hook_text: Make a map bigger on a photocopier. Which scale still tells the truth?
clip_script: Hogsback, a trail map for a school hike. The word scale says: one centimetre represents one kilometre. The line scale is a bar with marks: zero, one, two, three kilometres. Then the map is enlarged on a photocopier. Now the word scale is wrong, because one centimetre is not one kilometre any more. But the line scale grew with the map, so it is still correct. Word scale: easy to read. Line scale: always right.
visual_style: Whiteboard trail map with a word scale and a line scale, then a photocopier making it bigger, the word scale crossed out and the line scale glowing.
mood: Puzzling then satisfying, like solving a riddle.
pacing: Calm reading of each scale, a sudden photocopier twist, then the answer.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find the line scale on three maps in your atlas.
